title: Clamp LAN MSS on inbound share iface
description:
NAT rewrites the LAN source to the utun address before the current
`scrub out on $ext_if … from $int_if:network max-mss` can match. LAN
SYNs keep MSS 1460; fat TLS (Google/YouTube) RSTs. Mini-origin sockets
on the utun work because they inherit the tunnel MTU.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start tunshare against an AmneziaWG `utun` (MTU ~1376). Set Tunnel MTU to 1280 so pf shows `max-mss 1240`.
2. From a LAN client, open `https://ipleak.net/` (works) then `https://www.google.com/` (TLS RST).
3. `tcpdump -ni <utun> 'tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0'` shows the NAT'd SYN still advertising MSS 1460.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated pf clamps MSS on inbound LAN (`scrub in on $int_if … max-mss`), not on already-NAT'd `from $int_if:network` out the utun.
- WAN-bypass destinations are not clamped to the tunnel MSS.
- Belt clamp `scrub out on $ext_if … from ($ext_if)` still covers post-NAT SYNs.
- `just test` and `just lint` pass.

## Design

Primary: `scrub in on $int_if inet proto tcp from $int_if:network to any max-mss {mss}` (with bypass on: `to ! <tunshare_bypass>`).
Keep `scrub in all no-df`.
Drop `scrub out on $wan_if … max-mss`.
Optional belt: `scrub out on $ext_if inet proto tcp from ($ext_if) to any max-mss {mss}`.
close_reason: NAT rewrites LAN source before an outbound from-LAN clamp can match, so encapsulating tunnels RST fat TLS.

title: Fix LAN DNS SERVFAIL on NODATA/NXDOMAIN
description:
LAN :53 (in-process Hickory) maps every Resolver::lookup Err to SERVFAIL.
Hickory returns Err(NetError::Dns(DnsError::NoRecordsFound)) for NODATA and NXDOMAIN.
That forges failure for CNAME-of-an-A-name and poisons the negative cache.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start tunshare sharing so LAN DNS is 192.168.2.1:53.
2. `dig @1.1.1.1 gym.randomtools.download CNAME` → NOERROR, 0 answers, SOA.
3. `dig @192.168.2.1 gym.randomtools.download CNAME` → SERVFAIL.

## Acceptance Criteria
Vpn/Allow lookup Err(NoRecordsFound{NoError}) encodes NOERROR with empty answers (SOA in authority when present), not SERVFAIL.
Vpn/Allow lookup Err(NoRecordsFound{NXDomain}) encodes NXDOMAIN.
Timeout/IO/upstream SERVFAIL still encodes SERVFAIL and debug-logs qname, qtype, error.
Block still NXDOMAIN. Existing classify tests pass. No network in tests.
design: One encode_lookup_error on NetError for Vpn and Allow. Match NoRecordsFound response_code, copy SOA/authorities. Do not stringify before matching. Do not substring-match like status.rs is_nxdomain.
acceptance_criteria: Vpn/Allow NoRecordsFound NoError is NODATA not SERVFAIL; NXDomain is NXDOMAIN; timeout/IO/SERVFAIL still SERVFAIL and debug-logged; Block stays NXDOMAIN; unit tests no network.
close_reason: LAN DNS maps Hickory NoRecordsFound to NODATA/NXDOMAIN instead of SERVFAIL.

title: Own pf in com.tunshare; health re-hooks route-to
description:
## Problem

Live Mini: WAN NAT + persist table present, `pfctl -sr` had no `route-to`. Bypass IPs NAT onto en0 then follow utun4. `status --check` still green because it only tests A records vs the table.

Something else (Xray/NE, `pfctl -Fr`) rewrote MAIN filters. tunshare loaded MAIN with `pfctl -f` once and never re-checked. Health only probes utun + sysctl.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start sharing with WAN bypass on. Confirm `sudo pfctl -sr | grep route-to` and `WAN en0 via <gw>`.
2. Flush filters only: `sudo pfctl -Fr`.
3. Observe `pfctl -sn` still has `nat on en0 … to <tunshare_bypass>`, table still has IPs, `pfctl -sr` has no `route-to`.
4. Bypass sites fail or loop (IR traffic NATs to en0 then follows utun4). `tunshare status --check time.ir` can still print A records in the table.
5. Health stays Healthy until VPN drops; user must stop/start sharing to restore.

## Acceptance

- Sharing rules live in named pf anchor `com.tunshare` (NAT, rdr, filter, scrub). MAIN only has the hook lines (`nat-anchor` / `rdr-anchor` / `anchor`, plus `/*` children).
- Nested NAT-PMP is `com.tunshare/natpmp` (`pfctl -a com.tunshare/natpmp`), not a top-level `natpmp` hook.
- Health (existing 10s tick) verifies the bypass contract when WAN bypass is on: MAIN still has the three hooks; anchor body still has WAN NAT + `route-to ($wan_if $wan_gw)`. Miss → re-merge hooks and/or reload the body. Do not flush `<tunshare_bypass>`.
- `tunshare status` reads the anchor (`pfctl -a com.tunshare -sn/-sr`), not only MAIN. `no route-to` while prefs are on is a mismatch (and the heal target), not a silent hint.
- Stop: flush `com.tunshare` (and nested), strip tunshare hooks from MAIN. Do not `pfctl -f /etc/pf.conf` as the primary path (that stomps other writers). Fallback to `/etc/pf.conf` only if MAIN is empty of rules.
- WAN bypass scrub: `max-mss` on `$wan_if` as well as `$ext_if` (same generator).
- Unit tests: generated MAIN hooks vs body; NAT-PMP anchor path; status parser on unhooked MAIN + intact body; health/heal does not table_flush.
- Live: after a `pfctl -Fr`, next health tick restores `route-to` without a user restart. `status --check time.ir` still green AND `WAN … via <gw>` / `route-to en0`.

## Design

Approved approach: Anchor + health re-hook.

Start merges six hooks into current MAIN (snapshot + inject, never a canned MAIN replace). Body load is `pfctl -a com.tunshare -f`. Heal is the same merge + body reload if the contract string is missing. Table persist across heal.

Non-goals: lists UI overlay (mhh), UDP DNS spawn, HTTPS/CNAME table arming, changing WAN DNS upstream.
acceptance_criteria: Live: pfctl -Fr then next 10s tick restores route-to without a user restart. status reads the anchor and flags no route-to. NAT-PMP nested. Stop strips hooks, does not stomp MAIN via /etc/pf.conf. Table not flushed on heal. just check green.
notes: Claimed. Scratch: .beads/scratch/tunshare-0aa.md. Spec: ~/.factory/specs/2026-08-25-tunshare-0aa-pf-anchor-heal.md. Overlay mhh parked then restored. Clippy + 105 tests on HEAD+0aa then overlay restored.
close_reason: Sharing lives in com.tunshare. Health re-hooks MAIN and reloads the body without flushing the bypass table.

title: Pick source-internet WAN, skip share hairpin
description:
WAN bypass preferred Wi-Fi (`en1` → ASUS `192.168.50.1`). That gateway is already a neighbor on share `en8`, so IR `route-to` hairpins the USB NIC and Darwin panics (`dlil_input_en8`).

Hiddify/sing-box DIRECT binds the OS default NIC, skipping the TUN. tunshare analogue: skip utun, skip share iface, skip any ifscoped default whose gateway MAC appears on the share ARP table. Remainder on this Mini is `en0` → ONT.

No Wi-Fi preference.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable WAN bypass on the dual-homed Mini (share `en8`, Wi-Fi `en1` on ASUS LAN, ONT `en0`).
2. Query an IR name that hits bypass.
3. Observe pf `route-to (en1 192.168.50.1)` and `dlil_input_en8` panic under load.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `detect_wan_uplink` does not prefer Wi-Fi.
- An uplink whose gateway MAC is a neighbor on the share iface is skipped.
- `en0` → `192.168.254.1` still wins when Wi-Fi/ASUS LAN faces are present.
- Overlay files stay out of this change.
notes: Plan: .beads/scratch/tunshare-6q2.md. Branch: main. Overlay and lists.rs leftover stay out.
close_reason: detect_wan_uplink skips share-hairpin MAC; no Wi-Fi preference

title: Parse geosite TLD tokens so .ir hits WAN bypass
description:
chocolate4u ir.txt ships `domain:ir` and `domain:xn--mgba3a4f16a` as a whole-TLD bypass. tunshare `normalize_domain` drops names without a dot, so `snappfood.ir` never matches.

Honor `domain:<label>` with no dot (ASCII TLD or `xn--` punycode) in `DomainSet`. `contains_suffix` already walks to the last label.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable WAN bypass with chocolate4u `ir.txt`.
2. `tunshare status --check snappfood.ir`
3. Observe: neither Block nor WAN bypass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `domain:ir` and `domain:xn--mgba3a4f16a` parse into `DomainSet`.
- `contains_suffix("snappfood.ir")` is true when `ir` is in the set.
- Bare junk without `domain:` still dropped.
- Overlay / other dirty files not in this change.
notes: Plan: .beads/scratch/tunshare-64j.md. Branch: main. Overlay files stay out of this bead.
close_reason: Parse geosite TLD tokens; snappfood.ir suffix-matches domain:ir

title: WAN-bypass DoH on Wi-Fi (Cloudflare HTTPS)
description:
## Acceptance

WAN-bypass lookups use Hickory DoH (HTTPS to Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1, SNI cloudflare-dns.com) on BoundIfProvider sockets (IP_BOUND_IF on the WAN iface). No UDP/TCP :53 on WAN. VPN resolver stays Tokio UDP/TCP. DnsServer::start/attach_wan no longer take a WAN nameserver list; scutil resolver #1 is not used for WAN.

just check green.

Live proof (home Mini, after deploy): sudo tunshare status --check digikala.com returns A records and the bypass table contains them.

## Design

Approved spec: ~/.factory/specs/2026-08-24-wan-bypass-doh-on-wi-fi.md

Root cause: Wi-Fi :53 (UDP and TCP) is blocked even to the ISP router. TCP 443/853 on en1 with IP_BOUND_IF works. scutil resolver #1 is the VPN nameservers (wrong country if used on WAN).
notes: Claimed. Scratch: .beads/scratch/tunshare-rjn.md. Spec: ~/.factory/specs/2026-08-24-wan-bypass-doh-on-wi-fi.md. Overlay mhh parked in /tmp/tunshare-mhh.

description:

title: Fix MSS clamp black-hole: active path-MTU discovery + tunnel-MTU knob
description: pf scrub clamps MSS to interface_MTU-40, but ext_if is always a VPN tunnel whose interface MTU lies (OpenVPN-UDP reports 1500, real path MTU ~1440) -> full-size DF packets black-hole. Also the manual MTU knob was wired to en0, not the clamp/display, so the connection page always showed the raw upstream MTU. Fix: derive the clamp from real path MTU via an active DF-ping probe (Auto default), make it user-overridable (Fixed), always fall back to a conservative cap (never interface-40), and surface the effective MTU on the connection page. Repurpose LanMtu -> Tunnel MTU (drops the en0 mutation). Plan: ~/.claude/plans/bug-mss-clamp-derived-declarative-bear.md

Run: just run.

title: Add tunshare status live inspect command

`tunshare status` prints a live sharing snapshot from process + pf + config + list cache (no IPC). `tunshare status --check NAME` classifies against cached lists, queries LAN:53, and for WAN-bypass names expects the A records in `<tunshare_bypass>`.
Exit 0 consistent, 1 mismatch / leftover / unknown name, 2 listed-but-probe-failed. No clap. just status wrapper. README usage. just check green.

▎ Rust expert review — safety, async, idioms, error-surface, type-design

    If `TIMEOUT_LISTS` fires, `unwrap_or_default()` yields empty LoadedLists with no errors; `on_lists_refreshed` with `apply=true` then pushes empty DomainSets into the live resolver, _silently unblocking previously blocked names_.

—————— ▲ MAJOR · 11 ——————

1. `Idioms` — *src/app/async_ops.rs:903*
    `maybe_start_resolver` clones `block.set`/`allow.set` (_host-list sized_) into `ResolverLists` while still moving the `LoadedList`s.

2. `Safety` — *src/app/async_ops.rs:914*
    `ResolverStarted` keeps only counts/timestamps and _drops `LoadedList.errors`_, so startup fetch failures never reach the log.

3. `Async` — *src/app/async_ops.rs:1029*
    `Firewall::table_flush()` runs blocking `pfctl` inside the _async reload spawn_.

4. `Safety` — *src/app/result.rs:416*
    `on_firewall_reloaded` restores managers then applies `allowlist_on` with _no cancel guard_ (unlike `on_sharing_started`), so Esc during ReloadingFirewall can still turn WAN bypass on and persist it.

5. `Async` — *src/app/result.rs:487*
    `push_lists_to_resolver` `tokio::spawn`s a flag+set write and _drops the handle_; a stale spawn can overwrite a later master-toggle's `block_enabled`/`allow_enabled`.

6. `Safety` — *src/config.rs:360*
    `serde_json::from_str(&contents).unwrap_or_default()`: a single untagged `ListSource` that matches neither a string nor `{url, enabled}` fails the whole Config and _wipes unrelated prefs_ on next save.

7. `Async` — *src/system/lists.rs:72*
    `load_list` `join_set.spawn`s one task per URL with _no concurrency bound_.

8. `Safety` — *src/system/lists.rs:85*
    `JoinError` from a fetch task is `continue`d with no error recorded, so a panicked source _vanishes from the union_ and from `LoadedList.errors`.

9. `Async` — *src/system/lists.rs:118*
    `load_source` is async but `read_cache`/`fs::write`/`create_dir_all` are _blocking `std::fs`_ on the tokio runtime.

10. `Idioms` — *src/system/resolver.rs:274*
    `handle_query` clones both `DomainSet`s on every DNS query only to compute a `Decision`; _classify under the read lock_ instead.

11. `Async` — *src/system/resolver.rs:322*
    `Firewall::table_add` is blocking `pfctl` on the DNS query path inside `lookup_and_bypass`.

—————— ✜ MINOR · 7 ——————

1. `Idioms` — *src/app/input.rs:637*
    `activate_filter_row`/`remove_selected_custom` rebuild the full `filter_rows()` Vec just to _index the selected row_.

2. `Idioms` — *src/config.rs:208*
    `enabled_urls` clones every enabled URL into a new `Vec<String>` before `load_list` moves them into tasks.

3. `Safety` — *src/config.rs:212*
    `add_custom` returns `Result<(), String>` instead of a `std::error::Error` type.

4. `Safety` — *src/system/lists.rs:135*
    `let _ = fs::create_dir_all(parent)` discards cache-dir failure; only the later write is logged.

5. `Async` — *src/system/resolver.rs:83*
    resolver `tokio::spawn`s udp/tcp/evict loops without storing handles (_panics in those tasks are silenced_).

6. `Async` — *src/system/resolver.rs:210*

7. `Idioms` — *src/ui/lists.rs:98*

    Call sites pass `self.is_sharing()` as `refresh_lists_async`'s `apply` (`src/app/input.rs:546`) — reads as "refresh only if sharing", actually means _"also push to the live resolver"_.

ViewingLists handlers (`handle_lists_key`, `activate_filter_row`, `toggle_source`, `commit_custom_source`, `remove_selected_custom`) have zero tests; assigning `FilterRow::Add` to the wrong job or toggling the wrong source index would _ship green_.

`activate_filter_row`/`remove_selected_custom` rebuild the full `filter_rows()` Vec just to _index the selected row_.
`enabled_urls` clones every enabled URL into a new `Vec<String>` before `load_list` moves them into tasks.

`let _ = fs::create_dir_all(parent)` discards cache-dir failure; only the later write is logged.

`tcp_loop` spawns an _unbounded task per accepted connection_.
job titles allocate (`"Block".to_string()`, `"WAN bypass".to_string()`) on every painted row.
`reload_firewall_async`'s `allowlist_on` (`src/app/async_ops.rs:1007`) is another boolean that splits on vs off post-reload.

`filter_rows` (`src/app/state.rs:76`) rebuilds the whole tree on every key/draw with a copy-pasted Block then Allow loop.

Custom-label truncation uses a bare `40`/`39` (`src/config.rs:166`) with no named constant.
`ListSetting.enabled` comment (`src/config.rs:175`) still reads as if `enabled` avoids fetch, but `load_list` fetches enabled URLs _regardless of the job master_.
`remove_custom` (`src/config.rs:221`) returns `None` both for builtins and for a bad index, so callers cannot tell _why removal was a no-op_.
`last_fetch` fold (`src/system/lists.rs:97`) is an Option-max expressed as map+unwrap_or that would read clearer as a named `newest_fetch`.
Refresh is a single 90s spinner with elapsed seconds only; _no per-source progress_.
`l` for logs vs Domain filters · idle `l` expands logs, sharing `l` opens filters · cost: two products sharing a chord.
Space also toggles but no hint/help mentions it (in-card "Enter toggle", help "Enter: Toggle").
`x` removes a custom source with _no confirmation_.
Enter on an empty URL closes the add overlay with no success, error, or cancel acknowledgement.
"Using stale cached domain filters" has no retry hint (`r`).
"that URL is already in this list" lowercase, unlike "URL must start with...".
Footer "Enter toggle" is wrong on "Add source…" (Enter opens overlay) and never mentions add.
Owned builtins vs remote customs in one list · same ON/OFF source rows · cost: same chrome implies tunshare stands behind custom URLs the way it stands behind StevenBlack.
Unselected OFF badge uses `status_off` (DarkGray) on the default background; ON/OFF text is present so not color-only, but _contrast is weak_.
Job vs source hierarchy is indent-only (`"  "`), with no tree glyph (theme already has TREE_BRANCH).
Glanceable badge vs accurate job state · Domain filters menu value · cost: `off` hides that sources may still be enabled for the next ON.
`http://` acceptance (and trim-for-check/store-untrimmed) is untested; locking https-only in `is_http_url` would not fail `add_custom_rejects_non_http`.
`source_label` / 40-char custom truncation is untested; an off-by-one in `custom_source_label` would not fail any test.
`enabled_urls_skips_disabled_sources` asserts StevenBlack absent and `len() == 3` but not the three remaining URLs; skipping a different source plus adding a duplicate could still pass.
`remove_custom_keeps_builtins` asserts `remove_custom(0)` is None and length 4 after custom removal, not that the remaining URLs are the four builtins in order.

title: Add allow/block list support (split-tunnel + DNS blocking)
description:
Two independent settings:
- Blocklist: drops ad/tracker/malware domains via DNS NXDOMAIN
- Allowlist: routes matching domains' traffic out the LAN gateway instead of the VPN (split tunnel)

## List sources (chosen)
- Blocklist: StevenBlack/hosts + chocolate4u/Iran-v2ray-rules (ads.txt, malware.txt, phishing.txt)
- Allowlist: chocolate4u/Iran-v2ray-rules (ir.txt)

## Decisions made
- **Resolver approach (Q1):** custom Rust resolver using hickory-server + hickory-resolver. dnsmasq scope shrinks to DHCP-only.
- **Phasing (Q2):** single PR, blocklist + allowlist together.
- **Upstream for allowlisted domains (Q3):** WAN DNS (the LAN-side default resolver already discovered in dns.rs) — not VPN DNS, not a hardcoded IR resolver. Keeps DNS path aligned with traffic path so CDN steering returns correct nodes.

## Resolver decision tree
```
query for <domain>
  ├─ blocklisted?  → return NXDOMAIN
  ├─ allowlisted?  → forward to WAN DNS, capture response IPs → pf bypass table, return answer
  └─ otherwise     → forward to VPN DNS (current behavior)
```

## Implementation plan (8 steps)
1. **Config layer** — `~/.config/tunshare/config.toml` + `src/config.rs`. Schema with [lists.block] and [lists.allow] sections (enabled, sources, refresh_interval_hours). Sensible defaults baked in.
2. **List fetcher** — `src/system/lists.rs`. Fetch → cache to `~/.cache/tunshare/lists/<hash>.txt` → parse hosts/plain formats → two HashSet<String> (block, allow). Refresh on startup if >24h stale + manual trigger.
3. **Rust DNS resolver** — `src/system/resolver.rs`. Binds to LAN interface IP on :53 (not 0.0.0.0 — dodges mDNSResponder). Two upstreams (WAN DNS, VPN DNS). Implements decision tree. On allowlist hit, populates pf bypass table synchronously *before* returning answer (no race).
4. **dnsmasq scope shrinks** to DHCP-only (`--no-resolv --port=0`). Update `dhcp.rs`.
5. **pf bypass table + route-to** — `firewall.rs` gets `<tunshare_bypass>` table and rule `pass out on <vpn-if> route-to (<lan-if> <lan-gw>) from <lan-subnet> to <tunshare_bypass>`. New `pf_table_add(ips)` helper.
6. **TTL eviction** — flat 1h expiry, background task sweeps table.
7. **TUI Lists screen** — new state `ViewingLists` accessible from main menu. Shows per-list enabled/disabled, last fetch time, entry count. Actions: toggle, refresh-all.
8. **Cleanup on drop** — abort resolver task, flush pf bypass table, restore dnsmasq DNS role if changed.

## Open questions (decide before implementation)
- **Q4** — how to force LAN clients to use our resolver:
  - (a) DHCP-only (dnsmasq hands out our resolver IP) — doesn't catch static-IP clients
  - (b) Also add pf `rdr` rule redirecting `:53 from <lan-subnet>` → our resolver (recommended, catches hardcoded 8.8.8.8 users)
- **Q5** — bind resolver to LAN interface IP rather than 0.0.0.0 to dodge mDNSResponder on :53. Resolver serves LAN clients only, not the host. Confirm OK.
- **Q6** — should resolver run when DHCP is off? Likely yes, paired with Q4(b) rdr rule. Confirm.

## Risks / gotchas
- TTL precision: starting with flat 1h expiry; honoring real DNS TTLs is a v2 nicety.
- pf `route-to` requires LAN gateway IP — `network.rs` already partly detects this; may need a small extension.
- macOS mDNSResponder on :53 — bind to LAN IP specifically.
- First-connection race: handled by synchronous pf table update before DNS answer returns (the reason we picked custom resolver over a log-tailer).
- chocolate4u/StevenBlack URLs should be configurable via TOML, not hardcoded in source.

## Out of scope
- Per-client (per-LAN-device) rules
- TUI rule editor (lists are URL-driven; editing rules = editing TOML for now)
- Honoring real DNS TTLs for pf table eviction
- IPv6 (assume v4-only for v1; revisit if VPN/LAN both run v6)
